findings.title: Exited-wrapper descendants escape timeout cleanup and can survive reported PASS
findings.observed: Inherited pipe: wrapper exits0, timeout .2s leads unhandled second communicate TimeoutExpired after10.424s with live reparented child. Silent child: wrapper exits0, run_command reports PASS after.026s while child is still running. Reviewer killed only exact own child PID/start identity in both fixtures.
findings.impact: A prior stage-owned engine could remain alive while the next stage starts, violating serialized execution; failure/retry can leave untracked descendants.
findings.minimal_fix: Contain stage-owned descendants across parent exit without escaping canonical ROOT process-group ownership; cleanup/reap on success, failure and timeout; bounded structured failure and no next stage if cleanup cannot be proved. Preserve all original failures.
required_controls: parent exits nonzero with silent child

findings.title: Ambiguous/nonfinite/contradictory reports are accepted
findings.observed: Actual parser accepts contradictory duplicate passed=false/true, NaN metadata, nested command exit_code1 with passed=true, and a bare legacy [{passed:true}] without actual named command/check payload. Empty list and passed string controls correctly reject.
findings.minimal_fix: Strict decoded JSON keys/nonfinite rejection, consistent typed passed/exit metadata, and nonvacuous named command/check payload while preserving genuine legacy reports; add negative and valid-format controls.
